# Navigation[¶](#navigation "Permanent link")

A clear and concise navigation structure is an important aspect of good project documentation. Zensical provides several options to configure the behavior of navigational elements, including [tabs](#navigation-tabs) and [sections](#navigation-sections), as well as features such as [instant navigation](#instant-navigation) and [instant previews](#instant-previews).

Additional navigation can be configured [in the footer](../footer/#navigation).

## Configuration[¶](#configuration "Permanent link")

By default, Zensical creates the navigation sidebar on the basis of the folder structure and content of the Markdown pages. Likewise, it uses a default layout that can be overridden using various feature flags described on this page.

### Explicit navigation[¶](#explicit-navigation "Permanent link")

If you want to exercise more control over the structure of your navigation, you can create an explicit definition of the navigation structure in your configuration file. In the simplest case, you simply list the paths to your content files, leaving it to Zensical to extract a title for each of them from the content itself. The paths need to be relative to the [`docs_dir`](../basics/#docs_dir).

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)[project] [](#__codelineno-0-2)nav = [   [](#__codelineno-0-3)  "index.md",  [](#__codelineno-0-4)  "about.md", [](#__codelineno-0-5)]`

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)nav:   [](#__codelineno-1-2)  - index.md  [](#__codelineno-1-3)  - about.md`

Instead of letting Zensical figure out the title to use for the navigation entry for a page, you can also explicitly specify a title:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)[project] [](#__codelineno-2-2)nav = [   [](#__codelineno-2-3)  { "Home" = "index.md" },  [](#__codelineno-2-4)  { "About" = "about.md" }, [](#__codelineno-2-5)]`

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)nav:   [](#__codelineno-3-2)  - Home: index.md  [](#__codelineno-3-3)  - About: about.md`

#### Navigation sections[¶](#navigation-sections "Permanent link")

You can define navigation sections to create a navigation hierarchy that guides your users to the information they require.

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)[project] [](#__codelineno-4-2)nav = [   [](#__codelineno-4-3)  { "Home" = "index.md" },  [](#__codelineno-4-4)  { "About" = [    [](#__codelineno-4-5)    "about/index.md",    [](#__codelineno-4-6)    "about/vision.md",    [](#__codelineno-4-7)    "about/team.md",  [](#__codelineno-4-8)  ] }, [](#__codelineno-4-9)]`

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)nav:   [](#__codelineno-5-2)  - Home: index.md  [](#__codelineno-5-3)  - About:    [](#__codelineno-5-4)    - about/index.md    [](#__codelineno-5-5)    - about/vision.md    [](#__codelineno-5-6)    - about/team.md`

#### External links[¶](#external-links "Permanent link")

Navigation items typically provide a path to a Markdown page. However, any string that cannot be resolved to a Markdown page is treated as a URL.

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)[project] [](#__codelineno-6-2)nav = [   [](#__codelineno-6-3)  { "GitHub Repo" = "https://github.com/zensical/docs" }, [](#__codelineno-6-4)]`

`[](#__codelineno-7-1)nav:   [](#__codelineno-7-2)  - GitHub Repo: https://github.com/zensical/docs`

The "GitHub Repo" navigation entry takes the user to the repository for the Zensical Documentation.

### Instant navigation[¶](#instant-navigation "Permanent link")

When instant navigation is enabled, clicks on all internal links will be intercepted and dispatched via [XHR](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/XMLHttpRequest) without fully reloading the page. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-8-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-8-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-8-3)  "navigation.instant", [](#__codelineno-8-4)]`

`[](#__codelineno-9-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-9-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-9-3)    - navigation.instant`

The resulting page is parsed and injected and all event handlers and components are rebound automatically, i.e., **Zensical now behaves like a Single Page Application**. Also, the search index is persisted through navigation, which is especially useful for large documentation sites.

The [`site_url`](../basics/#site_url) setting must be set

Note that you must set [`site_url`](../basics/#site_url) when using instant navigation, as instant navigation relies on the generated `sitemap.xml` which will be empty if this setting is omitted.

#### Instant prefetching[¶](#instant-prefetching "Permanent link")

Instant prefetching is a new experimental feature that will start to fetch a page once the user hovers over a link. This reduces the perceived loading time for the user, especially on slow connections, as the page will be available immediately upon navigation. Enable it with:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-10-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-10-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-10-3)  "navigation.instant",  [](#__codelineno-10-4)  "navigation.instant.prefetch", [](#__codelineno-10-5)]`

`[](#__codelineno-11-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-11-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-11-3)    - navigation.instant    [](#__codelineno-11-4)    - navigation.instant.prefetch`

#### Progress indicator[¶](#progress-indicator "Permanent link")

In order to provide a better user experience on slow connections when using instant navigation, a progress indicator can be enabled. It will be shown at the top of the page and will be hidden once the page has fully loaded. You can enable it in your configuration with:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-12-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-12-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-12-3)  "navigation.instant",  [](#__codelineno-12-4)  "navigation.instant.progress", [](#__codelineno-12-5)]`

`[](#__codelineno-13-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-13-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-13-3)    - navigation.instant    [](#__codelineno-13-4)    - navigation.instant.progress`

The progress indicator will only show if the page hasn't finished loading after 400ms, so that fast connections will never show it for a better instant experience.

### Instant previews[¶](#instant-previews "Permanent link")

Instant previews allow the user to preview another site of your documentation without navigating to it. They can be very helpful to keep the user in context. Instant previews can be enabled on any header link with the `data-preview` attribute:

Link with instant preview

` [](#__codelineno-14-1)``` markdown [](#__codelineno-14-2)[Attribute Lists](#){ data-preview } [](#__codelineno-14-3)``` `

[Attribute Lists](../extensions/python-markdown/#attribute-lists)

Limitations

Instant previews are still an experimental feature and currently limited to headerlinks. This means, you can use them on any internal link that points to a header on another page, but not other elements with `id` attributes.

#### Automatic previews[¶](#automatic-previews "Permanent link")

The recommended way to work with instant previews is to use the Markdown extension that is included with Zensical, as it allows you to enable instant previews on a per-page or per-section level for your documentation:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-15-1)[project.markdown_extensions] [](#__codelineno-15-2)zensical.extensions.preview.configurations = [   [](#__codelineno-15-3)  {    [](#__codelineno-15-4)    targets.include = [      [](#__codelineno-15-5)      "customization.md",      [](#__codelineno-15-6)      "setup/extensions/*",    [](#__codelineno-15-7)    ]  [](#__codelineno-15-8)  }, [](#__codelineno-15-9)]`

`[](#__codelineno-16-1)markdown_extensions:   [](#__codelineno-16-2)  - zensical.extensions.preview:      [](#__codelineno-16-3)      configurations:        [](#__codelineno-16-4)        - targets:            [](#__codelineno-16-5)            include:              [](#__codelineno-16-6)              - customization.md              [](#__codelineno-16-7)              - setup/extensions/*`

The above configuration is what we use for our documentation. We've enabled instant previews for our changelogs, customization guide and for all Markdown extensions in the setup guide.

Full configuration example

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-17-1)[project.markdown_extensions] [](#__codelineno-17-2)zensical.extensions.preview.configurations = [   [](#__codelineno-17-3)  {    [](#__codelineno-17-4)    sources = {      [](#__codelineno-17-5)      include = [],      [](#__codelineno-17-6)      exclude = [],    [](#__codelineno-17-7)    }, # (1)!    [](#__codelineno-17-8)    targets = {      [](#__codelineno-17-9)      include = [],      [](#__codelineno-17-10)      exclude = [],    [](#__codelineno-17-11)    }, # (2)!  [](#__codelineno-17-12)  }, [](#__codelineno-17-13)]`

`[](#__codelineno-18-1)markdown_extensions:   [](#__codelineno-18-2)  - zensical.extensions.preview:      [](#__codelineno-18-3)      configurations:        [](#__codelineno-18-4)        - sources: # (1)!            [](#__codelineno-18-5)            include:              [](#__codelineno-18-6)              - ...            [](#__codelineno-18-7)            exclude:              [](#__codelineno-18-8)              - ...          [](#__codelineno-18-9)          targets: # (2)!            [](#__codelineno-18-10)            include:              [](#__codelineno-18-11)              - ...            [](#__codelineno-18-12)            exclude:              [](#__codelineno-18-13)              - ...`

1.  Sources specify the pages *on* which instant previews should be enabled. If this setting is omitted, instant previews will be enabled on all pages. You can use patterns to include or exclude pages. Exclusion is evaluated on top of inclusion, so if a page is matched by both, it will be excluded.
    
    Note that you can define multiple items under the `configurations` setting, which allows to precisely control where instant previews are shown.
    
2.  Targets specify the pages *to* which instant previews should be enabled. This is the recommended way to enable instant previews.
    

---

The [`site_url`](../basics/#site_url) setting must be set

Note that you must set [`site_url`](../basics/#site_url) when using instant previews, as instant previews rely on the generated `sitemap.xml` which will be empty if this setting is omitted.

### Anchor tracking[¶](#anchor-tracking "Permanent link")

When anchor tracking is enabled, the URL in the address bar is automatically updated with the active anchor as highlighted in the table of contents. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-19-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-19-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-19-3)  "navigation.tracking", [](#__codelineno-19-4)]`

`[](#__codelineno-20-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-20-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-20-3)    - navigation.tracking`

### Navigation tabs[¶](#navigation-tabs "Permanent link")

When tabs are enabled, top-level sections are rendered in a menu layer below the header for viewports above `1220px`, but remain as-is on mobile. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-21-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-21-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-21-3)  "navigation.tabs", [](#__codelineno-21-4)]`

`[](#__codelineno-22-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-22-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-22-3)    - navigation.tabs`

With tabsWithout

[![Navigation tabs enabled](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-tabs.png#gh-light-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-tabs.png#gh-light-mode-only) [![Navigation tabs enabled dark](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-tabs-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-tabs-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

[![Navigation tabs disabled](../../assets/screenshots/navigation.png#gh-light-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation.png#gh-light-mode-only) [![Navigation tabs disabled dark](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

#### Sticky navigation tabs[¶](#sticky-navigation-tabs "Permanent link")

When sticky tabs are enabled, navigation tabs will lock below the header and always remain visible when scrolling down. Just add the following two feature flags to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-23-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-23-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-23-3)  "navigation.tabs",  [](#__codelineno-23-4)  "navigation.tabs.sticky", [](#__codelineno-23-5)]`

`[](#__codelineno-24-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-24-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-24-3)    - navigation.tabs    [](#__codelineno-24-4)    - navigation.tabs.sticky`

### Navigation sections[¶](#navigation-sections_1 "Permanent link")

When sections are enabled, top-level sections are rendered as groups in the sidebar for viewports above `1220px`, but remain as-is on mobile. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-25-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-25-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-25-3)  "navigation.sections", [](#__codelineno-25-4)]`

`[](#__codelineno-26-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-26-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-26-3)    - navigation.sections`

With sectionsWithout

[![Navigation sections enabled](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-sections.png#gh-light-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-sections.png#gh-light-mode-only) [![Navigation sections enabled dark](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-sections-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-sections-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

[![Navigation sections disabled](../../assets/screenshots/navigation.png#gh-light-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation.png#gh-light-mode-only) [![Navigation sections disabled dark](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

Both feature flags, [`navigation.tabs`](#navigation-tabs) and [`navigation.sections`](#navigation-sections), can be combined with each other. If both feature flags are enabled, sections are rendered for level 2 navigation items.

### Navigation expansion[¶](#navigation-expansion "Permanent link")

When expansion is enabled, the left sidebar will expand all collapsible subsections by default, so the user doesn't have to open subsections manually. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-27-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-27-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-27-3)  "navigation.expand", [](#__codelineno-27-4)]`

`[](#__codelineno-28-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-28-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-28-3)    - navigation.expand`

With expansionWithout

[![Navigation expansion enabled](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-expand.png#gh-light-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-expand.png#gh-light-mode-only) [![Navigation expansion enabled dark](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-expand-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-expand-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

[![Navigation expansion disabled](../../assets/screenshots/navigation.png#gh-light-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation.png#gh-light-mode-only) [![Navigation expansion disabled dark](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

### Navigation path Breadcrumbs[¶](#navigation-path "Permanent link")

When navigation paths are activated, a breadcrumb navigation is rendered above the title of each page, which might make orientation easier for users visiting your documentation on devices with smaller screens. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-29-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-29-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-29-3)  "navigation.path", [](#__codelineno-29-4)]`

`[](#__codelineno-30-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-30-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-30-3)    - navigation.path`

With breadcrumbsWithout

[![Navigation path enabled](../../assets/screenshots/navigation.png#gh-light-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation.png#gh-light-mode-only) [![Navigation path enabled dark](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

[![Navigation path disabled](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-path.png#gh-light-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-path.png#gh-light-mode-only) [![Navigation path disabled dark](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-path-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-path-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

### Navigation pruning[¶](#navigation-pruning "Permanent link")

When pruning is enabled, only the visible navigation items are included in the rendered HTML, **reducing the size of the built site by 33% or more**. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-31-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-31-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-31-3)  "navigation.prune", # (1)! [](#__codelineno-31-4)]`

1.  This feature flag is not compatible with [`navigation.expand`](#navigation-expansion), as navigation expansion requires the complete navigation structure.

`[](#__codelineno-32-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-32-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-32-3)    - navigation.prune # (1)!`

1.  This feature flag is not compatible with [`navigation.expand`](#navigation-expansion), as navigation expansion requires the complete navigation structure.

This feature flag is especially useful for documentation sites with thousands of pages, as the navigation makes up a significant fraction of the HTML. Navigation pruning will replace all expandable sections with links to the first page in that section (or the section index page).

### Section index pages[¶](#section-index-pages "Permanent link")

When section index pages are enabled, documents can be directly attached to sections, which is particularly useful for providing overview pages. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-33-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-33-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-33-3)  "navigation.indexes", # (1)! [](#__codelineno-33-4)]`

1.  This feature flag is not compatible with [`toc.integrate`](#navigation-integration), as sections cannot host the table of contents due to missing space.

`[](#__codelineno-34-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-34-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-34-3)    - navigation.indexes # (1)!`

1.  This feature flag is not compatible with [`toc.integrate`](#navigation-integration), as sections cannot host the table of contents due to missing space.

In order to link a page to a section, create a new document with the name `index.md` in the respective folder, and add it to the beginning of your navigation section:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-35-1)[project] [](#__codelineno-35-2)nav = [   [](#__codelineno-35-3)  { "Section" = [    [](#__codelineno-35-4)    "section/index.md", # (1)!    [](#__codelineno-35-5)    { "Page 1" = "section/page-1.md" },    [](#__codelineno-35-6)    # ...    [](#__codelineno-35-7)    { "Page n" = "section/page-n.md" },  [](#__codelineno-35-8)  ] }, [](#__codelineno-35-9)]`

1.  `README.md` is also considered an index page.

`[](#__codelineno-36-1)nav:   [](#__codelineno-36-2)  - Section:    [](#__codelineno-36-3)    - section/index.md # (1)!    [](#__codelineno-36-4)    - Page 1: section/page-1.md    [](#__codelineno-36-5)    # ...    [](#__codelineno-36-6)    - Page n: section/page-n.md`

1.  `README.md` is also considered an index page.

### Table of contents[¶](#table-of-contents "Permanent link")

#### Anchor following[¶](#anchor-following "Permanent link")

When anchor following for the [table of contents](../extensions/python-markdown/#table-of-contents) is enabled, the sidebar is automatically scrolled so that the active anchor is always visible. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-37-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-37-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-37-3)  "toc.follow", [](#__codelineno-37-4)]`

`[](#__codelineno-38-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-38-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-38-3)    - toc.follow`

#### Navigation integration[¶](#navigation-integration "Permanent link")

When navigation integration for the [table of contents](../extensions/python-markdown/#table-of-contents) is enabled, it is always rendered as part of the navigation sidebar on the left. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-39-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-39-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-39-3)  "toc.integrate", # (1)! [](#__codelineno-39-4)]`

1.  This feature flag is not compatible with [`navigation.indexes`](#section-index-pages), as sections cannot host the table of contents due to missing space.

`[](#__codelineno-40-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-40-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-40-3)    - toc.integrate # (1)!`

1.  This feature flag is not compatible with [`navigation.indexes`](#section-index-pages), as sections cannot host the table of contents due to missing space.

With navigation integrationWithout

[![Navigation integration enabled](../../assets/screenshots/toc-integrate.png#gh-light-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/toc-integrate.png#gh-light-mode-only) [![Navigation integration enabled dark](../../assets/screenshots/toc-integrate-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/toc-integrate-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

[![Navigation integration disabled](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-tabs.png#gh-light-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-tabs.png#gh-light-mode-only) [![Navigation integration disabled dark](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-tabs-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)](../../assets/screenshots/navigation-tabs-dark.png#gh-dark-mode-only)

### Back-to-top button[¶](#back-to-top-button "Permanent link")

A back-to-top button can be shown when the user, after scrolling down, starts to scroll up again. It's rendered centered and at the bottom of the page. Add the following lines to your configuration:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-41-1)[project.theme] [](#__codelineno-41-2)features = [   [](#__codelineno-41-3)  "navigation.top", [](#__codelineno-41-4)]`

`[](#__codelineno-42-1)theme:   [](#__codelineno-42-2)  features:    [](#__codelineno-42-3)    - navigation.top`

## Usage[¶](#usage "Permanent link")

### Hide the sidebars[¶](#hide-the-sidebars "Permanent link")

The navigation and/or table of contents sidebars can be hidden for a document with the front matter `hide` property. Add the following lines at the top of a Markdown file:

`[](#__codelineno-43-1)--- [](#__codelineno-43-2)hide:   [](#__codelineno-43-3)  - navigation  [](#__codelineno-43-4)  - toc [](#__codelineno-43-5)--- [](#__codelineno-43-6)[](#__codelineno-43-7)# Page title [](#__codelineno-43-8)...`

### Hide the navigation path[¶](#hide-the-navigation-path "Permanent link")

While the [navigation path](#navigation-path) is rendered above the main headline, sometimes, it might be desirable to hide it for a specific page, which can be achieved with the front matter `hide` property:

`[](#__codelineno-44-1)--- [](#__codelineno-44-2)hide:   [](#__codelineno-44-3)  - path [](#__codelineno-44-4)--- [](#__codelineno-44-5)[](#__codelineno-44-6)# Page title [](#__codelineno-44-7)...`

## Customization[¶](#customization "Permanent link")

### Content area width[¶](#content-area-width "Permanent link")

The width of the content area is set so the length of each line doesn't exceed 80-100 characters, depending on the width of the characters. While this is a reasonable default, as longer lines tend to be harder to read, it may be desirable to increase the overall width of the content area, or even make it stretch to the entire available space.

This can easily be achieved with an [additional style sheet](../../customization/#additional-css) and a few lines of CSS:

`docs/stylesheets/extra.css``zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-45-1).md-grid {   [](#__codelineno-45-2)  max-width: 1440px; /* (1)! */ [](#__codelineno-45-3)}`

1.  If you want the content area to always stretch to the available screen space, reset `max-width` with the following CSS:
    
    `[](#__codelineno-46-1).md-grid {   [](#__codelineno-46-2)  max-width: initial; [](#__codelineno-46-3)}`
    

`[](#__codelineno-47-1)[project] [](#__codelineno-47-2)extra_css = [   [](#__codelineno-47-3)  "stylesheets/extra.css", [](#__codelineno-47-4)]`

`[](#__codelineno-48-1)extra_css:   [](#__codelineno-48-2)  - stylesheets/extra.css`

# Front matter[¶](#front-matter "Permanent link")

Zensical supports the inclusion of metadata in the front matter of a Markdown file that is stripped from the file contents before the rest of the content is handed over to the Markdown parser. It can be used in templates to customize rendering per-page.

## Page title[¶](#page-title "Permanent link")

This property overrides the page title in the navigation and in the `title` tag:

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)--- [](#__codelineno-0-2)title: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet [](#__codelineno-0-3)--- [](#__codelineno-0-4)[](#__codelineno-0-5)# Page title [](#__codelineno-0-6)...`

## Page description[¶](#page-description "Permanent link")

A Markdown file can include a description that is added to the HTML head `meta` tags of a page:

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)--- [](#__codelineno-1-2)description: Nullam urna elit, malesuada eget finibus ut, ac tortor. [](#__codelineno-1-3)--- [](#__codelineno-1-4)[](#__codelineno-1-5)# Page title [](#__codelineno-1-6)...`

## Page icon[¶](#page-icon "Permanent link")

Each page can define an icon that is displayed in the navigation, which must come from any of the [included icon sets](../icons-emojis/#included-icon-sets):

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)--- [](#__codelineno-2-2)icon: lucide/braces [](#__codelineno-2-3)--- [](#__codelineno-2-4)[](#__codelineno-2-5)# Page title [](#__codelineno-2-6)...`

## Page status[¶](#page-status "Permanent link")

A status can be assigned to each page, which is then displayed as part of the navigation sidebar. First, associate a status identifier with a description by adding the following to your configuration::

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)[project.extra.status] [](#__codelineno-3-2)<identifier>: "<description>"`

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)extra:   [](#__codelineno-4-2)  status:    [](#__codelineno-4-3)    <identifier>: <description>`

The identifier can only include alphanumeric characters, as well as dashes and underscores. For example, if you have a status `Recently added`, you can set `new` as an identifier:

`zensical.toml``mkdocs.yml`

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)[project.extra.status] [](#__codelineno-5-2)new = "Recently added"`

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)extra:   [](#__codelineno-6-2)  status:    [](#__codelineno-6-3)    new: Recently added`

`[](#__codelineno-7-1)--- [](#__codelineno-7-2)status: new [](#__codelineno-7-3)--- [](#__codelineno-7-4)[](#__codelineno-7-5)# Page title [](#__codelineno-7-6)...`

The following status identifiers are already defined:

-   – `new`
-   – `deprecated`

You can define a custom page status this way but if you want it to have an icon other than the default one you need to also configure that in your [`extra.css`](../../customization/#additional-css).

## Page template[¶](#page-template "Permanent link")

You can use the `template` metadata attribute to set a [custom template](../../customization/#custom-templates) for a page, which will be used instead of the default `main.html`. Note that you need to place the template you want to use in your [overrides directory](../../customization/#configuring-overrides), which needs to be configured before you can use it.

For example, to apply the `my_homepage.html` template to the page:

`[](#__codelineno-8-1)--- [](#__codelineno-8-2)template: my_homepage.html [](#__codelineno-8-3)--- [](#__codelineno-8-4)[](#__codelineno-8-5)# Page title [](#__codelineno-8-6)...`

## Hide sidebars[¶](#hide-sidebars "Permanent link")

Zensical allows you to hide elements of a page such as the navigation sidebar and the table of contents:

`[](#__codelineno-9-1)--- [](#__codelineno-9-2)hide:     [](#__codelineno-9-3)    - navigation    [](#__codelineno-9-4)    - toc [](#__codelineno-9-5)--- [](#__codelineno-9-6)[](#__codelineno-9-7)# Page title [](#__codelineno-9-8)...`

For more information about controlling search, see the [setup guide for search](../../setup/search/).

## Customization[¶](#customization "Permanent link")

### Use in templates[¶](#use-in-templates "Permanent link")

You can add further custom data to the front matter and use it in your [template overrides](../../customization/#template-overrides) or [custom templates](../../customization/#custom-templates). A common use case is to add metadata to the HTML `head`. Say you want to control whether a page is indexed by search engines by adding a [meta robots `nofollow` tag](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag).

The first thing you would need to do is to copy `main.html` to your [overrides directory](../../customization/#configuring-overrides) and add a [block override](../../customization/#overriding-blocks) for the `extrahead` block that adds a robots meta tag:

`[](#__codelineno-10-1){% extends "base.html" %} [](#__codelineno-10-2)[](#__codelineno-10-3){% block extrahead %}   [](#__codelineno-10-4)  {% if page and page.meta and page.meta.robots %}    [](#__codelineno-10-5)    <meta name="robots" content="{{ page.meta.robots }}" />  [](#__codelineno-10-6)  {% else %}    [](#__codelineno-10-7)    <meta name="robots" content="index, follow" />  [](#__codelineno-10-8)  {% endif %} [](#__codelineno-10-9){% endblock %}`

Note that the block override uses an `else` branch to set a default when the page metadata does not specify a value. Now, you can specify the robots meta tag content from the page header:

`[](#__codelineno-11-1)--- [](#__codelineno-11-2)robots: noindex, nofollow [](#__codelineno-11-3)--- [](#__codelineno-11-4)[](#__codelineno-11-5)# Page title [](#__codelineno-11-6)...`

### Use in plugins[¶](#use-in-plugins "Permanent link")

As Zensical approaches [feature parity](https://zensical.org/about/roadmap/#feature-parity) with Material for MkDocs, we will be adding modules that implement equivalent functionality and that make use of metadata.

display.text:
def render_engine_page(mod: str, rows: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> str:
    eng = MODULES[mod]
    title = TITLES[mod]
    cat = CATEGORY[mod]
    severity = SEVERITIES.get(mod, 'Warning')
    lines = [
        f'# {eng} - {title}',
        '',
        f'**Default severity:** {severity}',
        '**Auto-fix:** No',
        f'**Category:** {cat}',
        '**Can be disabled:** Yes',
        '',
        '## What this engine does',
        '',
        f'The `{eng}` rule implements the MATLAB Code Analyzer checks in the **{title}** category. All checks share one engine and are dispatched by tree-sitter node kind or by file-level traversal; each diagnostic carries the specific check ID (e.g. `{rows[0][0] if rows else "XXXX"}`).',
        '',
        '## Check IDs',
        '',
        '| Check ID | Description |',
        '| -------- | ----------- |',
    ]
    for cid, desc in rows:
        lines.append(f'| `{cid}` | {desc.replace("|", "\\\\|")} |')
    lines += [
        '',
        '## Configuration',
        '',
        '```toml',
        f'[lint.rules.{eng}]',
    ]
    if mod in ('performance', 'codegen', 'deployment', 'system_objects', 'unsupported'):
        lines.append('skip_checks = ["AGROW"]   # Turn off specific checks')
    else:
        lines.append('disabled_checks = ["XXXX"]   # Turn off specific checks')
    lines += [
        '```',
        '',
        'See [Configuration](configuration.md#per-engine-parameters) for the full parameter list and [rules.md](rules.md) for the complete rule inventory.',
        '',
    ]
    return '\n'.join(lines)


def write_engine_pages() -> int:
    for mod in MODULES:
        rows = CURATED.get(mod) or extract_table(mod)
        seen = set()
        rows = [r for r in rows if not (r[0] in seen or seen.add(r[0]))]
        page = render_engine_page(mod, rows)
        out = REPO / "docs" / f'{mod.replace("_", "-")}.md'
        out.write_text(page, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"wrote {out.name} ({len(rows)} checks)")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def main() -> int:
    args = set(sys.argv[1:])
    if "--print-data" in args:
        print(render_data_driven_tables(), end="")
        return 0
    if "--write-rules" in args or "--write" in args:
        rc = write_rules_md()
        if rc:
            return rc
    if "--write-pages" in args or "--write" in args:
        rc = write_engine_pages()
        if rc:
            return rc
    if not args:
        print(__doc__)
        return 0
    return 0

# COMPAT - Compatibility Considerations

**Default severity:** Warning
**Auto-fix:** No
**Category:** Compatibility
**Can be disabled:** Yes

## What this engine does

The `COMPAT` rule implements the **Compatibility Considerations** checks from MATLAB's Code Analyzer. It is a **data-driven** engine: check metadata (ID, message, severity) lives in `data/compatibility.toml` and is loaded into a lookup table at compile time.

On each `function_call` or `command` node the engine extracts the function name and performs an O(1) lookup. A matched name may produce **multiple** diagnostics (e.g. `tcpip` → TCPC + TCPS); every matching check ID is emitted.

On each `function_call` or `command` node the engine extracts the function name and performs an O(1) lookup. A matched name may produce **multiple** diagnostics (e.g. `tcpip` → TCPC + TCPS); every matching check ID is emitted.

I have the messages. Let me now form the plan. Let me think about what Phase 7 actually entails:

1. **Type inference pass** — a lightweight type-propagation over the symbol table:
   - Tracks variable types: logical, numeric, char/string, handle, cell, struct, unknown
   - Needed for: BDLGI (nonlogical operator sets a var), BDLOG1/2 (scalar logical expected in condition), BDSCA (operator in scalar context), BDSCI (nonscalar operator), MCHDP/MCHDT (property default is a handle)
   
2. **Cross-file / cross-scope resolver**:
   - SHVAU (shared variable confusion between parent/nested functions)
   - SHVAI (shared variable not explicitly defined in parent)
   - IDISVARHIGH/LOW (define-before-use in indexing)
   - GTARG/LTARG (function call arg count vs definition — needs to resolve function arity, possibly cross-file)
   - Cross-file analysis (resolving functions defined in other files)
   - Inline suppression `%#ok<RULE>`

Let me think about the realistic scope. This is the "last phase" so it's the full remaining ~13 checks + infrastructure + inline suppression + cross-file analysis.

Let me estimate the effort per check and design a plan.

Let me look at how the checks map to infrastructure needs:

**Type inference (5 checks):**
- BDLGI "Variable might be set by a nonlogical operator." — track variable types; if a variable used in a boolean/logical context is assigned a non-logical value, warn.
- BDLOG1 "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. Use 'any' or 'all'..." — in if/while condition, if a non-scalar logical variable used, warn.
- BDLOG2 "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression... or compare the scalar value to 0." — similar, scalar case.
- BDSCA "Unexpected use of VAR_OPERATOR in a scalar context." — operator applied to non-scalar.
- BDSCI "Variable might be set by a nonscalar operator." — variable set by operator producing non-scalar.

**Arity / cross-file (2 checks):**
- GTARG "Function might be called with too many arguments." — compare call arg count to callee signature.
- LTARG "Function might be called with too few arguments." — same.

**Handle detection (2 checks):**
- MCHDP "A property default value that is a handle will cause all instances to share the same object data."
- MCHDT "Declaring the value of a property as a handle might cause all instances to share the same default handle."
  These need: detect if a property default value is a handle class instance (e.g., `= SomeHandleClass()`), and the class type.

**Shared variable scope (3 checks):**
- SHVAU "Confusing usage of name VAR_NAME on lines X and Y. Initialize VAR_NAME before line X to make it a shared variable or rename..."
- SHVAI "Explicitly define shared variables in the parent function before calling the nested function."
- IDISVARHIGH "Variable must be explicitly defined before first use."
- IDISVARLOW "To avoid a potential conflict with functions on the path, explicitly define the variable before indexing into it."

**Infrastructure (2 items):**
- Inline suppression `%#ok<RULE>` — parse comment directives to suppress specific rules on lines.
- Cross-file analysis — resolve function definitions across files for GTARG/LTARG and general arity checking.

So Phase 7 = 13 checks + 2 infra items.

Let me think about the ordering/dependencies and what's realistic. The type-inference pass is the biggest lift. Let me think about a pragmatic design:

**Design: a lightweight type-inference module** `analysis/typing.rs`:
- A `TypeInfo` enum: Logical, Numeric, Char, String, Cell, Struct, Handle, FunctionHandle, Unknown.
- A per-variable type map built via a single pass over the AST: assign types from literals (`true/false` → Logical, numbers → Numeric, `'...'` → Char, `"..."` → String, `{...}` → Cell, struct literals → Struct), function calls (known constructors → Handle if class inherits handle), operators.
- Then the checks consume this.

4. **BDSCA** "Unexpected use of VAR_OPERATOR in a scalar context." — an operator used in a scalar context on an array.

5. **BDSCI** "Variable might be set by a nonscalar operator." — variable assigned from a nonscalar-producing operator.

6. **GTARG** "Function might be called with too many arguments." — a call passes more args than the callee's signature. Requires knowing callee arity → for local/same-file functions (resolvable from FunctionMeta/FileMeta), and for external functions requires cross-file or a known-signature table.

Let me think about what's realistic and give a well-structured plan. Let me also think about whether some of these checks can be done with simpler heuristics rather than full type inference.

Let me analyze each deferred check:

**BDLGI** "Variable might be set by a nonlogical operator." — When a variable is assigned from an expression using a nonlogical operator (like `+`, `*`) but then used in a logical context (like `if x`). Actually the message says "Variable might be set by a nonlogical operator." This fires when a variable is used in a conditional/logical context but was assigned via a non-logical operation.

**BDLOG1** "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar." — condition expression is a non-scalar logical array. E.g., `if x == y` where x,y are vectors.

**BDLOG2** "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar, or compare the scalar value to 0." — similar.

**BDSCA** "Unexpected use of VAR_OPERATOR in a scalar context." — an operator used in a scalar context (like `if A && B` where A is a matrix).

**BDSCI** "Variable might be set by a nonscalar operator." — variable assigned by an operator that yields nonscalar.

**GTARG** "Function might be called with too many arguments." — need function arity knowledge.

**LTARG** "Function might be called with too few arguments." — need function arity knowledge.

**MCHDP** "A property default value that is a handle will cause all instances to share the same object data." — property default value is a handle object.

**MCHDT** "Declaring the value of a property as a handle might cause all instances to share the same default handle." — similar.

**SHVAU** "Confusing usage of name VAR_NAME on lines VAR_NUMBER and VAR_NUMBER. Initialize VAR_NAME before line VAR_NUMBER to make it a shared variable or rename VAR_NAME on line VAR_NUMBER to disambiguate." — shared variable confusion between parent and nested functions.

**SHVAI** "Explicitly define shared variables in the parent function before calling the nested function. MATLAB does not share uninitialized variables between a nested function and the parent function." — shared variable defined in nested function but not initialized in parent.

**IDISVARHIGH** "Variable must be explicitly defined before first use. In some cases, the definition was not required in previous releases, but it is now required." — defined-before-use strictness.

**IDISVARLOW** "To avoid a potential conflict with functions on the path, explicitly define the variable before indexing into it." — indexing into a variable that could conflict with a function.

So the plan needs:
1. A type-inference pass (lightweight) — to track logical/numeric/scalar/handle/string types of variables.
2. A cross-scope shared-variable analysis — using the existing symbol table's scope tree.
3. Arity resolution for GTARG/LTARG — same-file resolution first (local functions, main function), then possibly builtin signatures.
4. Inline suppression `%#ok<RULE>` in the linter core.
5. Cross-file analysis — this is the big one; likely defer or scope minimally.

- **SHVAU/SHVAI**: need to identify shared variables between nested and parent functions and check initialization order. The symbol table already tracks scopes and nested functions. Feasible with a focused pass.
- **BDLGI/BDLOG1/BDLOG2/BDSCA/BDSCI**: need lightweight type inference (logical vs numeric, scalar vs nonscalar). This is the "type-propagation pass" — a new `analysis/typing.rs`.

Inline suppression `%#ok<RULE>` is a linter-core feature, independent of type inference.

In MATLAB, this fires when calling a function (typically a local/main function in the same file, or a known builtin) with an arity mismatch. Cross-file makes it hard. A reasonable scope: resolve against same-file functions (main, locals, methods) + a curated builtin signature table.

Let me also think about the type inference design more concretely since it's the core new infrastructure.

Type inference design:
- `analysis/typing.rs`
- Walk the AST, maintain a map of variable name → Type
- Type enum with scalar flag
- Rules:
  - `true`/`false` → Logical scalar
  - number literal → Numeric scalar
  - `'...'` → Char vector (nonscalar-ish)
  - `"..."` → String scalar
  - `[...]`/`{...}` → array/cell (nonscalar)
  - `x = a + b` → depends on a,b
  - `x = a > b` → Logical (scalar if a,b scalar)
  - `x = SomeClass()` → Handle (if SomeClass is a handle class)
  - `@(args)...` → FunctionHandle
  - `x = f(...)` → Unknown (unless known function returns known type)
  - comparisons (`==`, `~=`, `<`, etc.) → Logical
  - logical ops (`&&`, `||`, `&`, `|`, `~`) → Logical scalar (&&/||) or logical array (&/|)
- Then the checks:
  - BDLGI: in a conditional (`if x`), x was assigned via non-logical op → fire
  - BDLOG1: in `if x` where x is logical but non-scalar (array) → fire
  - BDLOG2: in `if x` where x is non-logical scalar → fire (compare to 0)
  - BDSCA: an operator like `&&`/`||` where an operand is non-scalar → fire
  - BDSCI: variable assigned from a nonscalar-producing op and used in scalar context

This is genuinely implementable as a conservative pass. Good.

For MCHDP/MCHDT: property default value that creates a handle (e.g., `= SomeHandleClass()`, or a handle object). Use metadata.all_properties() + check default_value text for handle-constructor pattern, and is_handle() on the class. Conservative.

For SHVAU: "Confusing usage of name on lines X and Y. Initialize before line X to make it shared or rename." This fires when a variable is used in a nested function AND in the parent with different meanings — specifically when a variable used in the parent function would be a shared variable with the nested function. The exact trigger: a nested function reads/writes a variable that is also defined in the parent, but the parent doesn't initialize it before the nested function is called, OR there's ambiguity. Conservative: detect a name used in both parent and nested function where the parent assignment occurs after the nested function definition. Fire.

For SHVAI: a shared variable used in a nested function that is NOT explicitly initialized in the parent before the nested call. Detect: nested function reads variable V; V is written in parent only after the nested function definition or never; fire.

For IDISVARHIGH: "Variable must be explicitly defined before first use." — a use (read) of a variable before any definition in the same scope, in a context where the analyzer is strict. This overlaps with NODEF. The distinguishing factor: it's the behavior-change version (some cases were allowed before). Conservative: reuse definite-assignment; fire where a variable is read before assignment but only for indexing/function-call-first-use patterns. Actually IDISVARHIGH vs IDISVARLOW distinction:
- IDISVARHIGH: must define before ANY first use (reading it as a value).
- IDISVARLOW: define before indexing into it (avoid function-on-path conflict).

So both can be built on the existing unset analysis. IDISVARLOW fires specifically when you index `x(i)` before x is defined (could be a function name). IDISVARHIGH fires for general read-before-def.

Now I'll write out the detailed plan for Phase 7. Let me structure it well.

Phase 7 has two parts per PLAN.md:
1. **Type inference** for 10 Good Practices checks + 3 generic compat unset checks (13 checks)
2. **Cross-file / cross-scope analysis** + **inline suppression** `%#ok<RULE>`

Let me categorize the 13 deferred checks by their infrastructure needs:

**Type-inference dependent (need `analysis/typing.rs`):**
- BDLGI "Variable might be set by a nonlogical operator." — track variable types; a var used in a boolean context was assigned a non-logical value
- BDLOG1 "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression." — condition is non-scalar logical (array)
- BDLOG2 "...or compare the scalar value to 0" — condition is a scalar that's not clearly logical
- BDSCA "Unexpected use of VAR_OPERATOR in a scalar context." — operator applied to a scalar-expected context where the operand might be non-scalar
- BDSCI "Variable might be set by a nonscalar operator." — var assigned from a nonscalar-producing operator used in scalar context
- MCHDP "A property default value that is a handle will cause all instances to share the same object data." — property default is a handle instance
- MCHDT "Declaring the value of a property as a handle might cause all instances to share the same default handle." — similar, handle-typed property default

**Cross-scope / shared-variable dependent (need scope analysis):**
- SHVAU "Confusing usage of name X on lines A and B. Initialize X before line A to make it a shared variable or rename X on line A to disambiguate." — nested function + parent both use a name ambiguously
- SHVAI "Explicitly define shared variables in the parent function before calling the nested function." — nested function reads parent var not initialized before call
- IDISVARHIGH "Variable must be explicitly defined before first use." — use-before-def strictness
- IDISVARLOW "To avoid a potential conflict with functions on the path, explicitly define the variable before indexing into it." — indexing into a name that might be a function

**Arity dependent (GTARG/LTARG):**
- GTARG "Function might be called with too many arguments." — needs callee signature (cross-file for external, or same-file for local/methods)
- LTARG "Function might be called with too few arguments."

**Infrastructure:**
- Type-propagation pass (`analysis/typing.rs`)
- Cross-scope/cross-file resolver
- Inline suppression `%#ok<RULE>` (linter core feature, not a rule)

Let me think about how to scope this realistically. Cross-file analysis is a huge lift. Let me propose a pragmatic split:

**Wave 7-A: Type-inference infrastructure** — new `analysis/typing.rs` module
- A `TypeInfo` lattice: Logical, Numeric, Char, String, Cell, Struct, Handle, FunctionHandle, Unknown
- Build a variable → type map by walking assignments
- Scalars vs arrays tracking
- This is the biggest single piece.

**Wave 7-B: Logical/operator checks** (BDLGI, BDLOG1, BDLOG2, BDSCA, BDSCI) — consume typing pass
- In good_practices, new check file `check_logical_usage.rs`

**Wave 7-C: Handle-default property checks** (MCHDP, MCHDT)
- In good_practices, new check file `check_handle_defaults.rs` — detect property default that instantiates a handle class (constructor call to a handle class), using metadata.is_handle() + typing

**Wave 7-D: Shared-variable scope analysis** (SHVAU, SHVAI, IDISVARHIGH, IDISVARLOW)
- Extend symbol table with shared-variable detection between parent/nested functions
- IDISVAR* in good_practices or the generic compat module? Actually IDISVARHIGH/LOW and SHVAI are in the generic compat module per PLAN (they're in compatibility.toml data). Wait — SHVAI/IDISVARHIGH/IDISVARLOW are in data/compatibility.toml with generic pattern. But SHVAU is a Good Practices check. Let me confirm.

Actually from PLAN.md Phase 7:
- Good Practices: BDLGI, BDLOG1, BDLOG2, BDSCA, BDSCI, GTARG, LTARG, MCHDP, MCHDT, SHVAU (10)
- Generic compatibility (unset vars): SHVAI, IDISVARHIGH, IDISVARLOW (3)

So SHVAU is Good Practices, SHVAI/IDISVAR* are generic compat.

**Wave 7-E: Arity checks** (GTARG, LTARG)
- Same-file resolution first: resolve call to local functions/methods/main function signatures using FunctionMeta
- Cross-file: a workspace resolver (larger) — or defer cross-file, do same-file only + a data table of common builtin arities

**Wave 7-F: Inline suppression `%#ok<RULE>`** — linter core

## Wave 7-A: Type-inference infrastructure (`analysis/typing.rs`)

**New module** `crates/mlt_rules/src/analysis/typing.rs`, exported from `analysis/mod.rs`.

**Design:**
- `TypeInfo` enum: `Logical`, `Numeric`, `Char`, `String`, `Cell`, `Struct`, `Handle`, `FunctionHandle`, `Unknown` + a `scalar: bool` flag.
- `TypeEnv::build(tree, source)` — one DFS pass mapping each variable to its inferred type:
  - literals: `true/false`→Logical, numbers→Numeric, `'...'`→Char, `"..."`→String, `{...}`→Cell, struct literal→Struct, `@(...)`→FunctionHandle.
  - assignments: `x = <expr>` — infer from RHS operator (comparison/boolean op→Logical, arithmetic→Numeric, `?class`/handle ctor→Handle).
  - `is_scalar(x)` helper using matrix/cell literal shape + operator semantics.
- **Conservative by default**: anything unprovable stays `Unknown`; checks only fire on provable cases.

**Verification:** unit tests for type lattice, `cargo build` + `cargo clippy` zero warnings.

---

## Wave 7-B: Logical/operator checks (5) → `good_practices/check_logical_usage.rs`

Consume `TypeEnv`. New file with 5 `pub(crate)` methods, dispatched from `check_file()` (or node-level `if_statement`/`while_statement`/assignment):

| Check | Detection |
|---|---|
| **BDLGI** | A variable used in a boolean context (if/while condition) was assigned from a non-logical operator (`x = a + b; if x`) |
| **BDLOG1** | Condition is a non-scalar logical array (`x` logical but `~isscalar`) — suggest `any`/`all` |
| **BDLOG2** | Condition is a scalar but not provably logical — suggest comparing to 0 |
| **BDSCA** | An operator (e.g. `&&`/`\|\|`) is applied to a non-scalar operand in scalar context |
| **BDSCI** | A variable assigned from a non-scalar-producing operator is used where a scalar is expected |

Each gated on `disabled_checks`; exact official messages; fires + not-fires tests.

---

## Wave 7-C: Handle-default property checks (2) → `good_practices/check_handle_defaults.rs`

| Check | Detection |
|---|---|
| **MCHDP** | A property default value is a handle instance (`Prop = SomeHandleClass()` or `= handle(...)`) where the class `is_handle()` — all instances share object data |
| **MCHDT** | A property declared with a handle type/validation where a handle default is assigned — sharing is intentional per Constant |

Uses `FileMeta.all_properties()` + `is_handle()` (already at `metadata.rs:1001`) + `TypeEnv` handle detection. File-level, dispatched from `check_file()`.

---

## Wave 7-D: Shared-variable / defined-before-use checks (4)

**D1 — SHVAU (Good Practices)** → `good_practices/check_shared_vars.rs`
Detect ambiguous shared-variable usage: a name used in a nested function and also in the parent function where the parent assignment *after* the nested-function definition makes the semantics ambiguous. Uses `SymbolTable` scope tree (already tracks `NestedFunction` scopes at `symbols.rs:113`).

**D2 — SHVAI / IDISVARHIGH / IDISVARLOW (generic compat)** → `compatibility/generic/check_unset_vars.rs`
- **SHVAI**: a variable shared with a nested function is read in the nested function but never explicitly defined in the parent before the nested call.
- **IDISVARHIGH**: variable read before any definition, in a context where a definition is now required (stricter than existing `NODEF` — fires where old releases allowed it).
- **IDISVARLOW**: a name is indexed (`x(i)`) before being defined — potential conflict with a function on the path.

Wired into `compatibility/generic.rs` `collect_file_checks` (file-level pass already exists for REDEFGI/REDEFGG/NSTIMP). Reuses `analyze_definite_assignment` (`control_flow.rs:323`).

## Wave 7-E: Arity checks (GTARG, LTARG) → `good_practices/check_arity.rs`

| Check | Detection |
|---|---|
| **GTARG** | Call passes more arguments than the callee accepts |
| **LTARG** | Call passes fewer arguments than the callee requires |

**Two-tier resolution:**
1. **Same-file** (primary): resolve callee to a local function / method / main function via `FileMeta.functions`/`local_functions`/`methods` — compare call arg count to `FunctionMeta.inputs.len()` (handles `varargin` → unknown, skip).
2. **Builtin arity table**: a small embedded data table (`data/arity.toml`) for ~50 common MATLAB builtins where arity is fixed (e.g. `sin(x)`, `sqrt(x)`) — reuse the data-driven TOML pattern.

Cross-file resolution deferred to Wave 7-G (see decision below).

## Wave 7-F: Inline suppression `%#ok<RULE>` (linter core)

**Location:** `mlt_core/src/linter.rs` (post-traversal filter, after severity stamping, before sort).

**Behavior (mirrors MATLAB):**
- Scan source for comment directives: `%#ok<ID>`, `%#ok<*ID*>`, `%#ok<*all*>`, `%#ok<ID1,ID2>`.
- Suppress diagnostics whose `line` matches the comment's line (MATLAB semantics: the directive applies to the line it's on).
- Respect engine check IDs: suppression key matches the diagnostic `rule_id` (specific ID, not engine meta-ID).

**Config:** `[lint]` opt-in flag (`inline_suppression = true`, default on) so it can be disabled.

**Verification:** CLI + unit tests in `mlt_core`; verify `NOSEMI` suppressed on a line with `%#ok<NOSEMI>`.

The largest item: a project-level index of function signatures from all `.m` files (for GTARG/LTARG on external calls, and CLSUNK-style path checks). You are implementing Phase 7 MATLAB Code Analyzer checks in the `mlt` Rust linter (repo: /home/watermarkhu/repositories/mlt). Work ONLY in `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices/` and `crates/mlt_rules/src/data/` (create `data/arity.toml`). Do NOT touch `compatibility/`, `mlt_core/`, or `analysis/typing.rs` (already built).

## Shared infrastructure already available

`crates/mlt_rules/src/analysis/typing.rs` (already merged) provides:
- `TypeEnv::build(tree, source) -> TypeEnv` (one-pass conservative type inference)
- `env.type_of(name) -> TypeInfo { kind: TypeKind, scalar: bool }`
- `TypeKind`: Logical, Numeric, Char, String, Cell, Struct, Handle, FunctionHandle, Unknown
- `env.is_logical_scalar(name)`, `env.is_logical(name)`

Also available: `crate::analysis::symbols::SymbolTable` (`SymbolTable::build(tree, source)`, scopes with `defs`/`uses`/`children`/`parent`, `NestedFunction` scope kind), `crate::analysis::metadata::FileMeta` (`.class`, `.functions`, `.local_functions`, `all_properties()`, `ClassMeta::is_handle()`, `FunctionMeta { name, inputs, outputs }`), and `crate::analysis::control_flow::analyze_definite_assignment`.

## Conventions (study first)

- Read `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices/mod.rs`: engine `GoodPracticesEngine`, config `GoodPracticesConfig { disabled_checks: Vec<String>, max_variable_name_length }`. Checks gate on `self.config.disabled_checks.iter().all(|c| c != "XXX")` (module's convention). File-level checks dispatched in `check_file()` (mod.rs:~687); node-level in `check()` (mod.rs:~616).
- Per-check files: `use super::*;` + `impl GoodPracticesEngine { pub(crate) fn check_xxx(...) -> Vec<Diagnostic> }` + `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` using `crate::test_util::{has_id, lint_file}` (or `lint_nodes`). Register via `mod check_xxx;` in mod.rs and add dispatch lines.
- Diagnostic: `mlt_core::Diagnostic { rule_id, message, severity: Severity::Warning, byte_range, line, column, fix: None }`.
- Example reference file: `crates/mlt_rules/src/good_practices/check_elarlog.rs` (if/while condition walk), `check_prop_validation.rs` (FileMeta/all_properties), `check_oop_practice.rs` (class walking).

## Checks to implement — ALL Severity::Warning, gated on disabled_checks, exact official messages

### New file `check_logical_usage.rs` — BDLGI, BDLOG1, BDLOG2, BDSCA, BDSCI

These consume `TypeEnv`. File-level: `pub(crate) fn check_logical_usage(&self, tree, source) -> Vec<Diagnostic>`. Build `let env = TypeEnv::build(tree, source);` once. Walk `if_statement`/`while_statement` condition expressions (and `switch_statement` for expression contexts) via a DFS, and `assignment` nodes.

1. **BDLGI** "Variable might be set by a nonlogical operator." — a variable used in a boolean condition (`if x`, `while x`) was assigned from a non-logical-producing operator. Detect: walk assignments, if RHS operator is arithmetic (binary_operator with `+ - * / ^ .* ./ .^` etc., not comparison/boolean) and the LHS identifier is later used as a bare condition, fire. Use `env` to confirm the var is NOT logical.
2. **BDLOG1** "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar." — condition is a logical variable/expr that is NOT scalar (`env.type_of(name).kind == Logical && !scalar`).
3. **BDLOG2** "A scalar logical value is expected in the conditional expression. Use 'any' or 'all' to reduce the array to a logical scalar, or compare the scalar value to 0." — condition is a scalar but not provably logical (kind != Logical, scalar true, e.g. numeric scalar in `if`).
4. **BDSCA** "Unexpected use of VAR_OPERATOR in a scalar context." — a `boolean_operator` / `boolean_operator_short` (`&&`, `||`) has a non-scalar operand. Replace VAR_OPERATOR with the operator text and VAR_NAME with the operand name.
5. **BDSCI** "Variable might be set by a nonscalar operator." — a variable assigned from an operator that produces a non-scalar (e.g. `x = a:b`, `x = [1 2 3]`, matrix multiplication) and later used in a scalar context (bare condition, index into scalar-expected spot). Conservative: fire when LHS assigned from a `range`/`matrix`/array-producing op and used in `if x`/`while x`.

For messages that use `VAR_NAME`/`VAR_OPERATOR`, substitute the actual names. Keep conservative — fire only on clear, provable cases. Fires + not-fires tests each.

### New file `check_handle_defaults.rs` — MCHDP, MCHDT

File-level, uses `FileMeta::build` + `TypeEnv`. Iterate `meta.all_properties()`:
6. **MCHDP** "A property default value that is a handle will cause all instances to share the same object data. To avoid sharing, create the property value in the constructor. For intentional sharing, consider using a Constant property." — a property default value (from `PropertyMeta.default_value`) is a handle instance: text starts with a known handle class name followed by `(`, or contains a constructor call to the file's own class (if `meta.class.is_handle()`), or `= handle(`, `= onCleanup(`. Fire on the property's byte_range.
7. **MCHDT** "Declaring the value of a property as a handle might cause all instances to share the same default handle. To avoid sharing, create the handle for this property in the constructor. To express that sharing is intentional, use the Constant property attribute." — a property whose default value expression names a handle-typed value (e.g. a `handle`-derived class instantiation) — fire when the default references a class that is a handle and is shared by default. Conservative distinction: MCHDP fires on direct handle instantiation as default; MCHDT fires when a handle is assigned to a property that MATLAB would otherwise share. If the two are hard to distinguish, implement MCHDP for the direct-constructor-as-default case and MCHDT for the case where the default is an identifier/expression that resolves to a handle (from TypeEnv) — document the heuristic.

Fires + not-fires tests.

### New file `check_shared_vars.rs` — SHVAU

8. **SHVAU** "Confusing usage of name VAR_NAME on lines VAR_NUMBER and VAR_NUMBER. Initialize VAR_NAME before line VAR_NUMBER to make it a shared variable or rename VAR_NAME on line VAR_NUMBER to disambiguate." — file-level. Use `SymbolTable`. Find a name that is BOTH used in a nested-function scope AND assigned in the parent scope where the parent assignment occurs AFTER the nested function definition (making it ambiguous whether the name is a shared variable or a separate local). Fire on the nested function's use of the name. Substitute VAR_NAME with the name; the two line numbers are the parent assignment line and the nested-function use line. Conservative: only fire when a nested function scope exists and the same name is assigned in the parent after the nested function's start line. Fires + not-fires tests (e.g. a nested function using a parent var assigned BEFORE the nested function should NOT fire; assign-after should fire).

### New file `check_arity.rs` — GTARG, LTARG (+ `data/arity.toml`)

9. **GTARG** "Function might be called with too many arguments."
10. **LTARG** "Function might be called with too few arguments."

Node-level or file-level (pick file-level for simplicity, or node-level on `function_call`). Two-tier resolution:
- **Tier 1 (same-file)**: build a map of callee name → `FunctionMeta` from `meta.functions` + `meta.local_functions` (+ `meta.class.methods` if present). For a `function_call` with an identifier callee that matches a same-file function, compare the call's named argument count to `func.inputs.len()`. Fire GTARG if args > inputs; LTARG if args < inputs AND the function has no `varargin`. Skip if the callee is unknown/not in the map.
- **Tier 2 (builtin table)**: `data/arity.toml` with `[[functions]] name = "..." min_args = N max_args = M` for ~50 common MATLAB builtins with fixed arity (sin, cos, sqrt, abs, exp, log, log10, floor, ceil, round, sign, sum, mean, median, std, var, min, max, prod, numel, length, size, ndims, isempty, isequal, isnan, isinf, isfinite, islogical, isnumeric, ischar, isstring, iscell, isstruct, isscalar, isvector, ismatrix, zeros, ones, eye, rand, randn, reshape, repmat, sort, unique, flip, flipud, fliplr, rot90, transpose, ctranspose, char, double, single, int8, int16, int32, int64, uint8, uint16, uint32, uint64, logical, find, diff, cumsum, cumprod, linspace, logspace, disp, fprintf, sprintf, strcmp, strcmpi, lower, upper, strtrim, deblank). Use a reasonable min/max per function (e.g. sin min=1 max=1; sum min=1 max=3; fprintf min=1 max=99; sprintf min=1 max=99; size min=1 max=2; disp min=1 max=1). Load via `include_str!` + `toml` (see how `compatibility/mod.rs` loads its data file, or `suggested_improvements.rs`). Match the call's named args against the table; skip when args within [min,max].
- **Documented limitation (IMPORTANT)**: cross-file resolution is NOT implemented (deferred). External calls not in same-file or the builtin table are skipped entirely. Add a module doc note stating this.

Fires + not-fires tests: same-file function too many/too few; builtin `sin(1,2)` fires GTARG; `disp()` fires LTARG; correct calls silent.

## Wiring

- Add `mod check_logical_usage; mod check_handle_defaults; mod check_shared_vars; mod check_arity;` to `good_practices/mod.rs` mod list.
- Dispatch: BDLGI/BDLOG1/BDLOG2/BDSCA/BDSCI (check_logical_usage) → `check_file()`; MCHDP/MCHDT → `check_file()`; SHVAU → `check_file()`; GTARG/LTARG → `check_file()` (or `check()` if node-level).
- Add `data/arity.toml` and load it inside `check_arity.rs`.

- `cargo build`
- `cargo test -p mlt_rules good_practices` — new + existing pass
- `cargo clippy --all-targets` — ZERO warnings
- Full `cargo test -p mlt_rules` at the end.

Files created/modified, per-check detection summary, tests added, final build/test/clippy results. Do NOT commit.

## Goal

Mirror MATLAB's inline suppression directive. A comment of the form `%#ok<RULE_ID>` on a line suppresses diagnostics for that rule on that line. Support forms:
- `%#ok<NOSEMI>` — suppress one rule
- `%#ok<*NOSEMI*>` — same (with optional surrounding `*`)
- `%#ok<*all*>` or `%#ok<*>...` — suppress ALL rules on the line
- `%#ok<NOSEMI,AGROW>` — comma-separated multiple rules
- `%#ok<*NOSEMI*>` — wildcard-matched prefix/suffix (match if the directive rule-id matches by prefix/suffix with `*`)

The directive applies only to the line it appears on (MATLAB semantics). Match against the diagnostic's `rule_id` (the specific check ID, e.g. "NOSEMI", not the engine meta-ID like "NOSEMI" engine or "SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE").

## Current code to study

- `crates/mlt_core/src/linter.rs` — `Linter::lint(source, file_path)` at ~line 63. Flow: parse → `traverse()` (node checks) → file-level checks → stamp severity → sort → return. Add an opt-in config flag `inline_suppression: bool` (default **true**) under `[lint]`. `LintSection` already has `exclude`, `rules`, `categories`. Prefer storing on `Linter` if `Linter::new` takes config; otherwise add a field and set it. Look at how `Linter::new` is called in main.rs and in `test_util`/tests.

339:     /// Create a new Linter with the given configuration
340:     ///
341:     /// # Arguments
342:     ///
343:     /// * `options` - Configuration object (see LinterConfig)
344:     ///
345:     /// # Example
346:     ///
347:     /// ```javascript
348:     /// const linter = new Linter({
349:     ///   disable: ["MD041"],
350:     ///   "line-length": 120
351:     /// });
352:     /// ```
353:     #[wasm_bindgen(constructor)]
354:     pub fn new(options: JsValue) -> Result<Linter, JsValue> {
355:         let linter_config: LinterConfig = if options.is_undefined() || options.is_null() {
356:             LinterConfig::default()
357:         } else {
358:             serde_wasm_bindgen::from_value(options).map_err(|e| JsValue::from_str(&format!("Invalid config: {e}")))?
359:         };
360:

386:     ///   return `"[]"` without linting.

388:     /// Returns a JSON array of warnings, each with:
389:     /// - `rule_name`: Rule name (e.g., "MD001")
390:     /// - `message`: Warning message

Adapted for mlt (a MATLAB linter, not markdown).

Key design decisions:
1. **Where does the wasm binding live?** rumdl has it in the same crate (`src/wasm.rs`) gated by a `wasm` feature. mlt is a workspace with mlt_cli/mlt_core/mlt_rules. Options:
   - A: Add `wasm.rs` to `mlt_rules` (the crate that has all the rules + Linter usage) with a `wasm` feature. But mlt_rules depends on mlt_core which has Linter. Actually the Linter is in mlt_core. `all_rules` is in mlt_rules. The lint entrypoint needs both.
   - B: Create a new crate `mlt_wasm` (or `crates/mlt_wasm`) that depends on both mlt_core and mlt_rules, with `wasm-bindgen`. This is cleaner — rumdl is a single crate, but mlt is a workspace, so a dedicated wasm crate mirrors rumdl's `src/wasm.rs` while respecting the workspace layout.
   
   I think a new crate `crates/mlt_wasm` is the cleanest. It would contain `lib.rs` with the `#[wasm_bindgen]` API, use `mlt_core::Config`, `mlt_rules::all_rules`, `RuleRegistry`, `Linter`.

   Actually wait — can a workspace member with `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]` and `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target work? Yes. wasm-pack builds a single crate. A new `mlt_wasm` crate is the right approach.

2. **The JS-facing API.** rumdl exposes:
   - `init()` — console_error_panic_hook setup
   - `Linter` class with `new(options: JsValue)`, `get_config_warnings()`, `check(content, path) -> String` (JSON), `fix(content, path) -> String`, `get_config()`, 
   - `get_version() -> String`
   - `get_available_rules() -> String`
   
   For mlt:
   - `Linter::new(options)` — parse a JS config object into mlt's `Config`. mlt's `Config` is built from `.mlt.toml` TOML. For JS, we need a `LinterConfig` deserializable struct (like rumdl's) that maps to mlt's Config — severity shorthand/table, categories, disabled_checks, etc. Simpler: accept a TOML string OR a JS object. rumdl uses `serde_wasm_bindgen` to deserialize a JS object into `LinterConfig`. We can do the same with a `LinterConfig` mirroring mlt's config surface.
   - `check(content: &str, path: Option<String>) -> String` — parse MATLAB, run rules, return diagnostics as JSON. mlt's `Diagnostic` has rule_id, message, severity, byte_range, line, column, fix. Note: fix ranges are byte offsets; need char-offset conversion for JS (like rumdl does `convert_warning_for_js`).
   - `fix(content) -> String` — apply fixes. mlt's `apply_fixes` is in mlt_cli/src/main.rs:189. Would need to move/share it or reimplement in mlt_wasm. Actually it's a free function in main.rs; better to move `apply_fixes` into mlt_core (a natural home) or duplicate. This is a refactor decision.
   - `get_version()` — from env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")
   - `get_available_rules()` — list rule IDs from `all_rules`/inventory.

3. **WASM build config.** Mirror rumdl:
   - `Cargo.toml`: `[lib] crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`, wasm deps (`wasm-bindgen`, `console_error_panic_hook`, `serde-wasm-bindgen`), `wasm` feature.
   - Makefile `build-wasm` target: `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown && wasm-pack build --target web --no-default-features --features wasm`
   - Note: tree-sitter-matlab — does it compile to wasm32? tree-sitter is pure Rust (C parser embedded), should compile for wasm32. Need to verify.

4. **npm package (`wasm-pkg/`).** Mirror rumdl:
   - `wasm-pkg/README.md` (API reference for mlt-wasm)
   - `wasm-pkg/package.json.tmpl` (name `mlt-wasm`, repo url, keywords)
   - CI: `wasm-pack build`, merge package.json, copy README/LICENSE into `pkg/`, publish to npm.

   - `<style>` block
   - `<script type="module">` that does `const mod = await import('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mlt-wasm/mlt_lib.js'); await mod.default(); const linter = new mod.Linter({}); ...` and calls `linter.check(content)` / `linter.fix(content)`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install mise-managed tools with retries, a per-attempt timeout, and
# recovery from corrupted rustup downloads.
#
# Usage: mise-install.sh [tool ...]
#   No arguments installs everything from .mise.toml; arguments are passed
#   to `mise install` verbatim (e.g. rust python uv pipx:maturin).
#
# Why this exists: plain `mise install` in CI has failed two distinct ways.
# A corrupted partial download in ~/.rustup/downloads makes every retry fail
# with "could not rename 'downloaded' file", and a stalled download hangs the
# job until the 6-hour workflow timeout. Each attempt therefore runs under a
# timeout, and the rustup download cache is cleared before retrying.
set -u

ATTEMPTS=3
ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_SECS=600
RETRY_DELAY_SECS=10

# GNU timeout when available (Linux, git-bash); gtimeout on macOS runners
# (coreutils); otherwise run unguarded rather than fail.
run_with_timeout() {
  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout "$ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_SECS" "$@"
  elif command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    gtimeout "$ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_SECS" "$@"
  else
    "$@"
  fi
}

for attempt in $(seq 1 "$ATTEMPTS"); do
  run_with_timeout mise install "$@" --yes
  status=$?
  if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
    exit 0
  fi
  if [ "$status" -eq 124 ]; then
    echo "Attempt $attempt timed out after ${ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_SECS}s" >&2
  else
    echo "Attempt $attempt failed (exit $status)" >&2
  fi
  # A failed or killed download can leave .partial files that poison every
  # subsequent attempt; clear them so the retry starts clean.
  rm -rf "${HOME}/.rustup/downloads" 2>/dev/null || true
  if [ "$attempt" -lt "$ATTEMPTS" ]; then
    echo "Retrying in ${RETRY_DELAY_SECS}s..." >&2
    sleep "$RETRY_DELAY_SECS"
  fi
done

echo "All $ATTEMPTS install attempts failed" >&2
exit 1

# mise configuration for rumdl development environment
# This file manages development tools and their versions

[env]
# Environment variables for the project
RUST_BACKTRACE = "1"

[tools]
# Rust toolchain - version matches rust-toolchain.toml
rust = "1.96.0"

# Python for maturin/python bindings
python = "3.12"

# UV - Fast Python package and tool manager
uv = "latest"

# maturin - Python/Rust build backend. Installed as a prebuilt PyPI wheel via
# the pipx backend (uv tool install) instead of a cargo: tool, which would
# compile maturin from source on every CI build job (~5-7 minutes each).
"pipx:maturin" = "latest"

actionlint = "latest"

# Development tools installed via cargo
"cargo:cargo-nextest" = "latest"
"cargo:cargo-watch" = "latest"
"cargo:cargo-binstall" = "latest"
"cargo:cargo-zigbuild" = "latest"  # For building static Linux binaries
"cargo:git-cliff" = "latest"        # Changelog generator from conventional commits

# Zig for cross-compilation (used by maturin)
zig = "0.13"

# Additional Rust development tools for dependency management
"cargo:cargo-edit" = "latest"     # For cargo add/rm/upgrade commands
"cargo:cargo-outdated" = "latest" # Check for outdated dependencies
"cargo:lychee" = "latest"         # Link checker for markdown files
# Optional: Security and dependency tools
# "cargo:cargo-audit" = "latest"    # Security audit dependencies
# "cargo:cargo-deny" = "latest"     # Lint dependencies

# Note: maturin is installed as a prebuilt wheel via the pipx backend above.
# Other Python packages (cffi, etc.) are installed separately as needed.

[settings]
# Experimental features
experimental = true

# Enable idiomatic version files (like rust-toolchain.toml)
idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools = ["rust"]

# Configure rust/cargo homes if you want isolation from system rust
# rust_cache_dir = "./.mise/rust"
# cargo_home = "./.mise/cargo"

[settings.cargo]
# Use cargo-binstall when available for faster installations
binstall = true

[tasks.setup]
description = "Set up the complete development environment"
run = """
echo "Setting up rumdl development environment..."
echo "Installing Rust toolchain and tools..."
mise install
echo "Installing Python tools with uv..."
uv tool install twine
echo "Development environment setup complete!"
echo ""
echo "Installed tools:"
mise list
echo ""
echo "Python tools:"
uv tool list
"""

[tasks.verify]
description = "Verify all tools are installed correctly"
run = """
echo "Verifying development environment..."

echo "Cargo version: $(cargo --version)"

echo "cargo-nextest version: $(cargo nextest --version)"
echo "maturin version: $(maturin --version)"
echo ""
echo "Running quick test to verify setup..."
make test-quick
"""

[tasks.ci]
description = "Run CI checks"
run = """
echo "Running CI checks..."
make fmt
make lint
make test-quick
"""

# Plan: mlt WASM build + Playground (mise-managed) + npm publish prep

## Decisions locked in
- **mise** for tools + project tasks (`.mise.toml` `[tools]` + `[tasks]`), replacing just/xtask.
- **Full parity with rumdl**: npm package `mlt-wasm`, docs load from jsDelivr CDN by default, with a local-build option.
- **Mirror rumdl's `LinterConfig`** JS surface.
- **New crate `crates/mlt_wasm`**.
- CI workflow named **`release.yml`**.
- **Prepare npm publish** (mirror rumdl's publish job; actual publish gated on credentials).

---

## 1. `.mise.toml` (new, repo root)

**`[tools]`** — add the wasm + node toolchain:
```toml
[tools]
"cargo:wasm-pack" = "latest"
node = "24"
```
(matches rumdl's CI node 24; `wasm-pack` via the `cargo:` backend — prebuilt via binstall, no source compile.)

**`[tasks]`** — the build/test/local-docs recipes (mise task syntax, mirroring the earlier Makefile/just plan):
```toml
[tasks.build-wasm]
description = "Build the browser/npm wasm package"
run = """
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown 2>/dev/null || true
wasm-pack build crates/mlt_wasm --target web --no-default-features --features wasm --out-dir wasm-pkg/pkg
"""

[tasks.test-wasm]
description = "Run the wasm binding host tests"
run = "cargo test --features wasm -p mlt_wasm"

[tasks.serve-local-wasm]
description = "Copy the local wasm build into docs/assets so the playground loads it locally"
run = """
mkdir -p docs/assets/mlt-wasm
cp -r wasm-pkg/pkg docs/assets/mlt-wasm
"""
```
Workflow: `mise run build-wasm`, `mise run test-wasm`, `mise run serve-local-wasm`.

## 2. `mlt_core` refactor (small)
- Move `apply_fixes` (`mlt_cli/src/main.rs:189`) → `mlt_core` as `pub fn apply_fixes(source, &[Diagnostic]) -> String` (new `crates/mlt_core/src/fix.rs`); update CLI.
- Promote `line_col_of` (`linter.rs:342`) → `pub fn position_of(source, byte) -> (line, column)` so the wasm binding can compute `end_line`/`end_column`.
- Verify `cargo test`.

## 3. New crate `crates/mlt_wasm`
```
crates/mlt_wasm/
├── Cargo.toml   # [lib] name="mlt_lib", crate-type ["cdylib","rlib"],
│                #   wasm-pack profile wasm-opt=false, [features] wasm, workspace member
└── src/lib.rs   # #[wasm_bindgen] Linter + free fns + LinterConfig + host tests
```
- Optional deps: `wasm-bindgen`, `serde-wasm-bindgen`, `console_error_panic_hook`; required: `mlt_core`, `mlt_rules`, `serde`, `serde_json`.
- API mirrors rumdl `wasm.rs`: `init()` (start), `Linter::new(JsValue)` → `mlt_core::Config` → `active_rules` → `RuleRegistry` → `Linter`; `check(content, path?) → JSON` (rule_id, message, severity, line, column, end_line, end_column, fix); `fix(content, path?) → String`; `get_config_warnings()`, `get_version()`, `get_available_rules()`.
- `LinterConfig` mirrors rumdl (`disable`, `enable`, `fixable`, `unfixable`, `exclude`, `#[serde(flatten)] rules`).
- `#[cfg(test)]` host tests (run via `mise run test-wasm`).

## 4. `wasm-pkg/`
- `README.md` — `mlt-wasm` API reference (MATLAB-flavored; adapted from rumdl's).
- `package.json.tmpl` — name `mlt-wasm`, repository `watermarkhu/mlt`, keywords (matlab, linter, wasm, webassembly, lint, static-analysis). Version inherited from the merged `pkg/package.json` at publish time.

## 5. CI `release.yml`
Mirror rumdl's wasm job + publish, using mise and our task names:
- `mise setup` / `mise run build-wasm` (dtolnay/rust-toolchain with `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target).
